full_judgment: The Act was intended to remain for a period of three years from its commencement under sub-section (3) of section 1 of the Act. After omission of that sub-section by section 2 of Act IX of 1950 the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 got a place on the Statute Book. The Criminal Law Amendment Act of 1948 (Act XIX of 1948) was passed as a complementary to that law. That Act was replaced and repealed by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act of 1958 (Act XL of 1958) "for the more speedy trial and more effective punishment of certain offences", containing both procedural and substantive provisions. The Special Judge who administers Act II of 1947 is appointed under Act XL of 1958. Section 5 provides for the offences that are to be tried by him and a schedule of offences was appended to the Act.
